claims.text: Gas-phase oxidation selectivity on Pd nanoparticles is governed by preferential exposure of specific crystallographic facets.
Cubic Pd nanoparticles predominantly expose {100} facets.
Spherical Pd nanoparticles expose a mixture of facets.
Predominantly {100}-faceted cubic Pd nanoparticles provide adsorption sites distinct from those on spherical Pd nanoparticles.
The distinct adsorption sites on cubic Pd nanoparticles enhance oxidation-product selectivity relative to spherical Pd nanoparticles.
The cubic and spherical Pd samples will be synthesized with matched overall particle size.
Ligand-directed wet-chemical synthesis will be used to produce cubic Pd particles with predominant {100} facets and spherical Pd particles with mixed facets.
The comparison will be conducted in a gas-phase oxidation environment at 100–200 °C under identical flow conditions.
Particle size, catalyst loading, residual ligand content, and dispersion will be controlled between the cubic and spherical samples.
TEM with facet indexing and LEED can verify the distinct exposed crystallographic facets.
Controlling the listed non-facet variables would ensure that any selectivity difference is due solely to facet orientation.
The nature and distribution of Pd surface facets modulate reactant adsorption energies.
Facet-dependent surface atomic configurations alter oxidation reaction pathways and thereby alter product selectivity.
Cubic Pd nanoparticles are predicted to show statistically significantly higher selectivity for the designated oxidation product than spherical Pd nanoparticles.

The hypothesis is restricted to cases in which particle-size distribution, residual ligands, dispersion, and other parameters are equivalent and the reaction remains within 100–200 °C in a gas-phase oxidation environment.
Minor differences in particle size or residual capping ligands may affect catalytic performance.
Failure of cubic particles to show statistically significantly higher selectivity, or failure of selectivity to correlate with {100}-facet density, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The structural-mediator field says that the controls ensure selectivity differences are due solely to facet orientation, while the uncertainty field acknowledges that residual ligand and particle-size variations may still affect performance. The latter prevents the claimed sole-cause attribution unless those confounders are demonstrated to be equivalent.
